content.text:
`python3 -m unittest -q` now passes (all 7 tests). I fixed two bugs in `household/bills.py` and changed one expected value in a test.

**Code fixes:**
1. **`split_bill` lost the leftover cents.** It gave everyone `total // people` and dropped the rest. Now the leftover cents go one each to the first people, as the docstring says. For example, `split_bill(1001, 2)` → `[501, 500]`.
2. **`due_dates` broke across a new year.** It added to the month number without moving on to the next year, so a November start produced month 13 and an `IllegalMonthError`. It now goes from December to January of the next year correctly.

**Test change:** In `tests/test_bills.py`, `test_three_ways` expected `split_bill(1000, 3)` to return `[333, 333, 333]`, which only adds up to 999 cents. That clashes with the docstring and with `test_remainder_goes_to_the_first`, so no correct version of the function could pass both tests. I changed the expected result to `[334, 333, 333]`. If you actually want the leftover cent dropped, tell me and I'll switch it back. That would mean changing the docstring and the other test too.

Nothing is committed.
